title: Launch Ops decision canvas and sprint cadence negotiator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a decision canvas artifact and an associated sprint-cadence negotiation workflow to coordinate multi-surface launches (runtime, console, API). The goal is to provide a single canonical place for teams to: 1) reserve launch windows, 2) declare capacity/traffic contracts, 3) set decision-lattice rules for rollback/rollforward, and 4) surface telemetry gates that map to SLOs. This reduces last-minute cutover disputes, speeds cross-team approvals, and makes trade-offs explicit (latency vs cost vs coverage).
updates: 2026-02-18 - Maya Chen: Draft created. Outlined core problem: frequent last-minute cadence conflicts and ambiguous rollback ownership across runtime/console/api. Proposed a lightweight artifact (decision canvas) + meeting SLA for cadence negotiation.

2026-02-24 - Rafael Ortega: Met with Eng infra and Console PMs to validate fields needed on the canvas. Key asks: capacity hedge (GPU slots), regional blackout windows, automated telemetry hooks, and a clear escalation path if SLO regressions occur during cutover.

2026-03-02 - Design review with Lina Park: Proposed canvas layout for rapid scanning (left: timeline & reservations, center: contracts & owners, right: telemetry/gates & rollback rules). Lina will produce a Figma quick mock for the war room view by 2026-03-09.
2026-03-05 - Eng feedback (from ENG-1842 thread): Runtime team requests an explicit model-variant compatibility matrix and a fallback lane tag for each reservation. Added to canvas fields.

2026-03-11 - PM sync: Agreed on pilot with runtime + console teams for April sprint cutover. Action items: finalize canvas template, add calendar-as-code schema, and implement a lightweight dashboard to show live signals during the week-of-launch. Assigned follow-ups below.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas template completed and reviewed by runtime, console, and api PMs and design
Calendar-as-code schema defined (JSON/YAML) and a sample reservation created via a PR
Pilot run scheduled for a single April launch; pilot participants confirmed and slots reserved
Runbook documenting negotiation meeting cadence, escalation flow, and telemetry gate thresholds published
Lightweight dashboard (Grafana panel) showing the three primary signals (latency p99, error rate, capacity utilization) for pilot week
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Teams treat the canvas as advisory not binding -> Mitigation: Add sign-off requirement for reservations above P1 impact and enforce capacity commitments in the sprint planning ritual.
Risk: Telemetry gates trigger overly conservative rollbacks -> Mitigation: Define banded thresholds (warning/soft-fail/hard-fail) and require runbook actions for each band.
Risk: Calendar-as-code schema version drift across teams -> Mitigation: Versioned schema with compatibility rules and a linter in the launch-cadence repo.
Risk: Lack of on-call availability during cutover -> Mitigation: Pre-assign on-call stewards and a fast-escalation Slack channel documented in the canvas.
next_steps: Infra: Add telemetry hooks to pilot dashboard (ENG-1842) by 2026-03-20
PM: Publish canvas template to Confluence and open calendar-as-code PR by 2026-03-16
